extracted.intended_audience: NRC stakeholders: nuclear power plant licensees, applicants, industry groups, technical staff, and members of the public preparing comments
extracted.subtask_description: A proposed NRC rule to incorporate by reference IEEE Std 603-2018 into 10 CFR part 50, specifying applicability, limited regulatory requirements from the standard (notably Clause 5.16), conforming amendments, and related procedural analyses and guidance. The document solicits public comment and describes availability of materials and supporting guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation by reference of IEEE Std 603-2018 into 10 CFR 50.55a
rubrics_metrics.description: The NRC proposes to revise §50.55a to add paragraph (a)(2)(v) and to reference IEEE standard 603-2018 (IEEE Std 603-2018), “Standard Criteria for Safety Systems for Nuclear Power Generating Stations” (Approval date: September 27, 2018). All other standards that are referenced in IEEE Std 603-2018 are not approved for incorporation by reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the central regulatory change: add IEEE Std 603-2018 as an incorporated standard for protection and safety systems; the proposal includes specific regulatory text to be added to §50.55a. The rule would specify which applicants/licensees must meet the standard based on filing/permit dates (see applicability criteria).

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory requirement from Clause 5.16 (Common-cause failure)
rubrics_metrics.description: When applying IEEE Std 603-2018, the first sentence within Clause 5.16, 'Common-cause failure,' captures the only regulatory requirement of Clause 5.16: that the safety system design and development shall address common-cause failures (CCFs) that create a potential to degrade or defeat the safety system function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The NRC considers the remainder of Clause 5.16 to be guidance on ways to address CCF. Methods described in Clause 5.16 may be acceptable as part of D3 (defense-in-depth and diversity) analyses but are not comprehensive; licensees/applicants may also use other methods (e.g., Draft Regulatory Guide DG-1251, NUREG-0800 BTP 7-19, SRM-SECY-22-0076). Each identified source of CCF should be evaluated case-by-case; risk-informed approaches may credit low consequence/low likelihood conclusions in plant-specific analyses consistent with NRC policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability by construction-permit and application filing dates
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed rule specifies differential applicability: (i) For plants with construction permits issued after Jan 1, 1971, but before May 13, 1999, protection systems must meet IEEE Std 279-1968/279-1971 or IEEE Std 603-1991 (with correction) or IEEE Std 603-2018; (ii) For plants with construction permits issued before Jan 1, 1971, protection systems must be consistent with their licensing basis or may meet IEEE Std 603-1991 (with correction) or IEEE Std 603-2018; (iii) Applications filed on or after May 13, 1999 but before the final rule effective date must meet IEEE Std 603-1991 (with correction) or IEEE Std 603-2018; (iv) Applications filed on or after the effective date (30 days after final rule publication) must meet IEEE Std 603-2018.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proposed rule defines effective dates and crosswalks between legacy standards and IEEE 603-2018 to identify which standard applies to which application/license based on dates. The proposed effective date for the final rule is 30 days after publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and scope of 'safety system' and 'safety function' (per IEEE Std 603-2018)
rubrics_metrics.description: IEEE Std 603-2018 defines 'safety system' as a system relied upon to remain functional during and following design-basis events to assure (a) integrity of the reactor coolant pressure boundary, (b) capability to shut down and maintain safe shutdown, or (c) capability to prevent or mitigate accidents that could result in potential offsite exposures comparable to regulatory guidelines. 'Safety function' examples include emergency negative reactivity insertion, post-accident heat removal, emergency core cooling, post-accident radioactivity removal, and containment isolation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The NRC recognizes that 'protection systems' are a subset of 'safety systems' and that using the terminology in IEEE Std 603-2018 does not change the scope of systems covered in currently operating plants' final safety analysis reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk-informed alternatives to Clauses 5.3 and 5.4 under 10 CFR 50.69
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed conforming amendment to paragraph (b)(1)(v) of §50.69 would extend that provision to allow risk-informed alternatives to Clauses 5.3 and 5.4 of IEEE 603-1991 and Clauses 5.3 and 5.4 of IEEE 603-2018 for certain structures, systems, and components.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paragraph (b)(1)(v) would list the inservice testing and inspection requirements and electrical component quality/qualification requirements, and explicitly include Clauses 5.3/5.4 of the IEEE standards as eligible for risk-informed alternatives for certain SSCs as incorporated in §50.55a(h).

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation by reference — reasonable availability to interested parties
rubrics_metrics.description: The OFR regulations (1 CFR part 51) require a proposed rule to discuss how incorporated material is reasonably available to interested parties; the NRC must distinguish classes of interested parties and explain availability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The NRC identifies classes of interested parties (small and large entities, NGOs, other federal/state/local bodies, Indian Tribes, members of the public) and states availability via: the NRC Technical Library (by appointment), ADAMS public documents collection, purchase from IEEE Standards Association website, or third-party subscription services (e.g., Accuris IHS). The NRC concludes the material is reasonably available to interested parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntary consensus standards policy (NTTAA) and invitation to comment
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the National Technology Transfer and Advancement Act, Federal agencies should use technical standards developed by voluntary consensus bodies when practicable. The NRC proposes to incorporate the voluntary consensus standard IEEE Std 603-2018 and invites comment on the applicability and use of other standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This frames the rule as consistent with federal policy favoring voluntary consensus standards and requests stakeholders' input on alternative standards or applicability concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of guidance (Draft Regulatory Guide DG-1251, Revision 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: The NRC is issuing draft guidance DG-1251, Revision 1, 'Guidance for the Power, Instrumentation, and Control Portions of Safety Systems for Nuclear Power Plants' to accompany the proposed rule and provide additional guidance for implementing the requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DG-1251 is based on the proposed rule discussion and does not modify the scope of §50.55a(h). The NRC requests public comment on the draft regulatory guide; DG-1251 and related documents are available via ADAMS (accession numbers provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Backfitting and issue finality — no backfit for existing licensees
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the NRC's Backfit Rule (10 CFR 50.109), backfitting is limited by statutory standards. The NRC states this proposed rule would not constitute backfitting because it would not change requirements for existing licensees or applicants; it allows voluntary compliance with IEEE Std 603-2018 for existing licensees/applicants requesting changes, and would require new applicants/licensees to meet IEEE Std 603-2018 after the effective date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Backfit is defined in §50.109(a)(1); the proposed approach treats the rule as applicable to new approvals and voluntary for existing facilities making changes, thus avoiding backfit implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory Flexibility Certification (Economic impact on small entities)
rubrics_metrics.description: As required by the Regulatory Flexibility Act, the NRC certifies that this rule, if adopted, will not have a significant economic impact on a substantial number of small entities because it affects only licensing and operation of nuclear power plants and plant owners do not meet the definition of 'small entities'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This certification is made under 5 U.S.C. 605(b) and references NRC size standards (10 CFR 2.810). The NRC requests comment on the draft regulatory analysis examining costs and benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environmental Assessment and Proposed Finding of No Significant Environmental Impact
rubrics_metrics.description: The NRC determined under NEPA and its regulations that this rule, if adopted, would not be a major Federal action significantly affecting the quality of the human environment, and therefore an environmental impact statement is not required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: the proposed rule does not significantly increase accident probability/consequences, does not change effluent types, and does not significantly increase public radiation exposure. Stakeholders may comment on any aspect of the environmental assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paperwork Reduction Act — no new collections of information
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed rule does not contain any new or amended collections of information subject to the Paperwork Reduction Act; existing collections are approved by OMB under specified control numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites OMB approval numbers (3150-0011, 3150-0264, 3150-0151) and includes the standard public protection notification about OMB control numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public participation — how to obtain information and submit comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Instructions for obtaining information and submitting comments: use Docket ID NRC-2024-0045 on Regulations.gov; access documents via ADAMS; contact NRC PDR or Technical Library by appointment; submit comments by Regulations.gov, email, fax, mail, or hand delivery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The NRC encourages electronic submission via Regulations.gov, requests inclusion of Docket ID in comments, cautions commenters not to include identifying/contact information they do not want publicly disclosed (comments will be posted and entered into ADAMS), and gives contact details for questions and document access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public meeting notice and procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: The NRC will conduct a public meeting to describe the incorporation by reference of IEEE 603-2018; staff will be available to answer questions. The NRC will publish notice of location, time, and agenda in the Federal Register, on Regulations.gov, and on the NRC public meeting website at least 10 calendar days before the meeting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stakeholders should monitor the NRC public meeting website for updates and will be informed of agenda and logistics; the meeting is to promote understanding and facilitate comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope clarification — referenced standards not incorporated unless approved
rubrics_metrics.description: IEEE Std 603-2018 references several industry codes and standards that are not proposed for incorporation by reference; these referenced standards are not mandatory NRC requirements. If a referenced standard has been endorsed in a regulatory guide, the standard constitutes a method acceptable to the NRC for meeting a regulatory requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proposed rule explicitly states that 'All other standards that are referenced in IEEE Std 603-2018 are not approved for incorporation by reference.' This clarifies that only IEEE Std 603-2018 itself is being incorporated, not its external references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conforming text changes to 10 CFR parts (§50.55a, §50.69, Appendix E)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section-by-section proposed revisions: revise §50.55a paragraphs (a)(2) add (v); revise introductory text to (h) and paragraphs (h)(2) and (h)(3) to include IEEE Std 603-2018 and to repeat the Clause 5.16 first-sentence requirement; revise §50.69(b)(1)(v) to reference Clauses 5.3 and 5.4 of IEEE 603-1991 and IEEE 603-2018; revise Appendix E footnote 7 title from 'Protection Systems' to 'Protection and safety systems.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Federal Register preamble includes the exact regulatory text proposed for insertion or revision to the CFR to effect incorporation and conforming edits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency with NRC/C o mmission policy on CCF and risk-informed approaches (SRM-SECY-22-0076 and SRM-SECY-98-144)
rubrics_metrics.description: The NRC states that the Clause 5.16 first-sentence requirement is consistent with Commission policy on CCF (SRM-SECY-22-0076). The Commission approved expanded acceptance of risk-informed approaches for D3 assessments and in determining adequacy of design, prevention, and mitigation measures for postulated digital I&C CCF.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Licensees/applicants may use Clause 5.16 methods and other referenced methods (DG-1251, NUREG-0800 BTP 7-19, DRG) in D3 analyses; risk insights must be considered with other factors in a risk-informed approach, as required by SRM-SECY-98-144 and SRM-SECY-22-0076.
